text: In May of 2014, thirty-nine of us said "national defense authorization," and thirty-eight said "national defense authorization act," peaking together on the twenty-second. That same day twenty-nine of us reached for "usa freedom act," twenty-eight for "the usa freedom act." At the end of the month our language turned: thirty-six of us said "secretary eric shinseki" on the thirtieth, while twenty-six said "veterans affairs secretary" and twenty-four "secretary of veterans affairs." Twenty-four of us said "water resources reform" on the twentieth. We record that these were our most-repeated phrases and that we said them in these numbers, on these days, together. We do not here characterize why the count on "secretary eric shinseki" rose as the month closed. We report only that it did, and that we were the ones who said it.
